content:
ana: heads up — noticed our onboarding sample app is occasionally creating duplicate tasks when we hit 429s during auth refresh. not full outage but annoying for customers :grimace:

mike: hmm — is that when the sdk retries silently after refresh? any logs?

ana: yes. sequence: 1) refresh token fails 429, sdk retries refresh (backoff) 2) refresh succeeds on retry, app code replays original request which the sdk also retried, so double side-effect. stack: node js sdk, single-endpoint POST /tasks

sam: can you paste minimal logs? curious if the sdk emitted any idempotency header or replay guard.

ana: paste below, redacted keys:

```
[2030123456] request POST /tasks body={..} -> 429 RefreshThrottle
[2030123457] sdk: starting token refresh
[2030123458] refresh attempt 1 -> 429
[2030123460] refresh attempt 2 -> 200 token_ok
[2030123461] app: retrying original request (app-level retry)
[2030123462] sdk: outgoing POST /tasks (no idempotency header)
[2030123463] tasks created id=abc123
```

mike: ok that makes sense — two separate retries: one from token refresh path and one from app. we need a safe-replay signal or an SDK-level replay suppression. current SDK allows a config `unsafeReplay: boolean` but default is permissive for backwards compat. code path probably doesn't attach X-Idempotency-Key automatically.

jess: for the sample app we should do two things: 1) attach idempotency header from app for mutating ops 2) reduce refresh-retry aggressiveness or add jitter probe so refresh failures don't overlap with app retry window. also add telemetry so we can detect duplicate side-effects.

mike: agree. proposed quick patch for sdk default: enable a short dedupe window for the same client-generated idempotency key when refresh occurs. Pseudocode:

```
// on send(request)
if (!request.headers['Idempotency-Key']) {
  request.headers['Idempotency-Key'] = generateWeakKey(request)
  request._generatedBySdk = true
}
// on retry after refresh: if _generatedBySdk and within dedupeWindow -> suppress client re-send
```

sam: careful: generated keys could mask legitimate retries across a cluster. prefer app-supplied keys for strong dedupe. SDK-generated keys should be opt-in, or weak by namespace + timestamp. also need to document parity across node/go/python.

ana: for immediate mitigation in the sample app we added a short client-side debounce: if original request got 429 and we're in token refresh window, wait jittered 100-400ms before app retry. that prevented one duplicate during manual testing.

jess: bump: what jitter strategy? full jitter vs equal jitter? our other threads favored full jitter (sleep = random(0, base * 2^attempt)), but for small debounce a bounded uniform random might be simpler.

mike: i'd use full jitter for refresh attempts, and uniform jitter for app-level debounce. Example backoff config we landed on for sample app:

```
refresh.backoff = { base_ms: 50, max_ms: 2000, strategy: 'full_jitter', max_attempts: 3 }
app.retry_debounce = { min_ms: 100, max_ms: 400 }
```

sam: we should also expose metrics: "sdk.replay_guard.suppressed", "app.duplicate_side_effects.count", and emit event when we detect created resource with recent same request hash. that will help detect regressions.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled for canary at 2030123600 — CI green: all tests passed :white_check_mark:

ana: followups: 1) can we add a sample snippet in onboarding docs showing Idempotency-Key usage? 2) small SDK patch to opt-in auto-idempotency for mutating endpoints behind a feature flag?

jess: yes to both. i'll add a docs blurb and the feature flag `sdk.autoIdempotency=false` default false. will also add a note about parity: go/python/node should implement same flag name and behavior.

mike: want me to open the SDK PR with tests for the dedupe window and a small integration test with the sample app?

ana: please. include a tiny harness that simulates refresh 429 + app retry and assert only one create call to backend. that would have caught this earlier.

sam: can we add a lint rule in sample app CI to forbid mutable POSTs without an Idempotency-Key header? maybe as a test, not lint.

jess: good idea. i'll add a test in the sample-app repo that fails on missing Idempotency-Key for POST /tasks.

ana: thanks all. i'll update the onboarding issue with the mitigation and link the PRs once created. :pray:

mike: thx — quick win.

ci-bot: comment: created ticket RW-5256 "sdk: opt-in auto idempotency + dedupe window" assigned to @mike

ana: noted. closing the immediate incident (not a user-facing outage) but logging for follow ups.
